ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a heating curve, with the vertical axis being Temperature (°C) and the horizontal axis being Heat added (kcal/mol). The curve first rises from about -50°C to about 10°C, and is briefly horizontal near 10°C; then it rises to 75°C and remains at a longer horizontal plateau at 75°C; finally it rises again to 125°C. Reasoning: In a heating curve, the boiling point corresponds to the temperature of the upper horizontal plateau when liquid changes into gas. In the figure, the upper long horizontal plateau is at 75°C, so the boiling point of this substance is 75°C.

method.method_draft: First inspect the heating curve: temperature rises, levels off briefly near 10°C, rises again, then stays flat for a long interval at 75°C before rising to 125°C. From the question, the requested quantity is the boiling point. Use the heating-curve rule that the boiling point is the temperature of the upper horizontal plateau where liquid changes to gas. Therefore read the boiling point as 75°C.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph axes: temperature in °C on the vertical axis and heat added on the horizontal axis. Identify the red heating curve and note its horizontal segments, especially the long upper plateau at 75°C.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question wording to know that the target is the boiling point of the hypothetical substance, not the melting point or another temperature.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: On a heating curve, a horizontal plateau indicates a phase change at constant temperature. The lower plateau corresponds to melting/freezing, while the higher-temperature plateau corresponds to boiling/condensation.
